newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki stocks limp to weak pre-Fed close.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki stocks limp to weak pre-Fed close.

text.p: Shares ended off after a numb and exceptionally thin session on Monday, with activity curbed by the dual brakes of a key Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday and a holiday in many European markets, brokers said.

The HEX fell 1.24 percent to 3,026.40 in skimpy 165 million markka volume, taking an early downward cue from Wall St on Friday and with no top-board issues repeating gung-ho gains that at least helped Nokia in the latter part of last week.
"Tomorrow is a little more viable because the European operators are back," one broker said.
Nokia was especially thin, slipping 5.00 markka to 334.00.

A potential source of action on Tuesday was Enso, due to report Q1 results with no year-ago data yet available: "Its volatility will anyway raise tomorrow," said one broker. Enso dipped 1.00 markka to 46.00 in extremely thin trade.

With trade largely limited to domestic players there was price action in less well-known issues like newspaper Ilkka, which was very thin but ended at a new year-high of 205.00 markka, up 16.00 markka or over eight percent.
One broker cited possible speculation amid a broader reorganisation of media in Finland.
